exam_scheme.note: PSTET (Punjab State Teacher Eligibility Test) is conducted by the State Council of Educational Research and Training (SCERT), Punjab in coordination with the Punjab School Education Board (PSEB), SAS Nagar (Mohali), under the guidelines framed by the National Council for Teacher Education (NCTE). The test is administered to determine eligibility for appointment as teachers in primary (Classes I-V) and upper primary (Classes VI-VIII) schools across Punjab. The examination consists of two objective OMR-based papers: Paper I (for Primary Stage) and Paper II (for Upper Primary Stage). Candidates seeking eligibility for both levels may appear in both papers. All questions are multiple-choice objective type carrying 1 mark each with no negative marking.

stages.stage_name: PSTET Paper I (Primary Stage: Classes I to V)
stages.source_label: SCERT Punjab / PSEB PSTET Official Information Bulletin & Guidelines

papers.paper_name: Paper I: Complete Objective Test (5 Compulsory Sections of 30 MCQs Each)
papers.negative_marking: No negative marking (0 marks deducted for incorrect responses)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 60% (90 marks out of 150) for General (UR) category candidates; minimum 55% (82 marks out of 150) for SC, ST, OBC/BC, and Differently Abled candidates per NCTE and Punjab Government norms. Comprises Child Development & Pedagogy (30 Qs / 30 marks), Language I Punjabi (30 Qs / 30 marks), Language II English (30 Qs / 30 marks), Mathematics (30 Qs / 30 marks), and Environmental Studies (30 Qs / 30 marks).

stages.stage_name: PSTET Paper II (Upper Primary Stage: Classes VI to VIII)
stages.source_label: SCERT Punjab / PSEB PSTET Official Information Bulletin & Guidelines

papers.paper_name: Paper II: Complete Objective Test (Core Pedagogy & Languages + Subject Specialization)
papers.negative_marking: No negative marking (0 marks deducted for incorrect responses)
papers.qualifying_threshold: Minimum 60% (90 marks out of 150) for General (UR) category candidates; minimum 55% (82 marks out of 150) for SC, ST, OBC/BC, and Differently Abled candidates per NCTE and Punjab Government norms. Comprises Child Development & Pedagogy (30 Qs / 30 marks), Language I Punjabi (30 Qs / 30 marks), Language II English (30 Qs / 30 marks), and Subject Specialization (60 Qs / 60 marks in Mathematics & Science for Math/Science teachers OR Social Studies / Social Science for Social Studies teachers).

competition_benchmarks.note: PSTET serves as the mandatory qualifying benchmark for teacher recruitment in Punjab Government schools (Master Cadre, ETT Cadre), government-aided schools, and private recognized schools under the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009. In accordance with NCTE guidelines, the PSTET qualifying certificate is valid for a lifetime.
